editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a house where everyone is lying to each other while a father waits to die. You get to meet Brick, a former football star who does nothing but drink whiskey and stay angry. His wife, Maggie, is desperate for his love and wants to have a baby, but Brick just pushes her away. The whole movie feels like a pressure cooker because the family is forced to face truths they have hidden for years. It is a heavy story about regret and the things people say when they have nothing left to lose.

Elizabeth Taylor is incredible here, and you can really feel her frustration. The dialogue is sharp and hits hard, though the movie moves slowly since most of it happens in one room. If you like deep character studies, you will love this. Just make sure you are in the mood for some serious family drama before you hit play.
endingExplained: At the end, the lies finally fall apart. Brick admits that he loved his friend Skipper and that Skipper likely loved him back. He realizes his own fear of those feelings is why he stopped playing football and started drinking. While the father dies believing a lie about his health, Brick and Maggie find a small bit of hope. They decide to try and fix their marriage, though the sadness of the past still hangs over them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strong acting and family secrets.
